requirement_paraphrase: Robustness is the combination of integrity and assurance and equals the lower of the two (Table 1). Low assurance is a declaration by the applicant; medium needs supporting evidence, typically testing or operational data; high needs verification by a competent third party.

Guidance (4.2.4): when determining the operational volume the applicant should consider position keeping in 4D, including accuracy of the navigation solution, flight technical error, path definition (map) error and latencies.

requirement_paraphrase: SORA is a recommended methodology to establish confidence that a specific operation can be conducted safely: ConOps evaluation, categorisation into six SAIL levels, then recommended operational safety objectives per SAIL.

requirement_paraphrase: Robustness = lower of integrity and assurance level. Low assurance: applicant declares; medium: applicant supplies evidence (testing/operational data); high: verified by a competent third party. Three robustness levels (low, medium, high).

requirement_paraphrase: Documentation of the operation: maps and data for ground/air risk, flight profiles incl. nominal, contingency and emergency phases, mitigations, contingency volume and ground risk buffer and how they were determined.

requirement_paraphrase: Intrinsic GRC from max UA characteristic dimension/speed and highest population density in the footprint (operational volume plus ground risk buffer). UA of 250 g or less and 25 m/s or less gets iGRC 1; combinations without an iGRC are outside SORA (certified category). Guidance (4.2.4) says the operational volume should account for navigation solution accuracy, flight technical error, path definition (map) error and latencies.

requirement_paraphrase: Optional ground-risk mitigations lower the GRC: M1(A) sheltering -1 (low) / -2 (medium); M1(B) operational restrictions -1 (medium) / -2 (high); M1(C) ground observation -1 (low); M2 impact reduction -1 (medium) / -2 (high). Final GRC above 7 is out of SORA scope (certified category).

requirement_paraphrase: Initial ARC (a-d) from airspace; strategic mitigations give residual ARC; TMPR is none/low/medium/high for ARC a/b/c/d. VLOS is an acceptable tactical mitigation for all ARC levels; BVLOS segments need TMPR with matching robustness (detect-and-avoid for higher ARC).

requirement_paraphrase: SAIL from final GRC and residual ARC: e.g. GRC 5 with ARC a/b/c/d gives IV/IV/IV/VI; GRC 6 gives V/V/V/VI; GRC 7 gives VI; GRC above 7 is certified category. SAIL sets OSO robustness levels and evidence expected.

requirement_paraphrase: Containment: for UA of less than 250 g, containment is low with no adjacent-area limits. Otherwise the adjacent area extends the distance flown in 3 minutes at max UA speed (bounded 5-35 km); containment robustness (low/medium/high) derives from allowed population density, assemblies within 1 km, UA size and SAIL.

Examples: OSO#06 (C3 link) NR/L/L/M/H/H; OSO#04 (airworthiness design standard) NR/NR/NR/L/M/H; OSO#24 (adverse environmental design) NR/NR/M/H/H/H.
